Article Title: Nitin Gadkari says India is sending Rs 22 lakh crore out of country to import petrol, diesel, and gas; pushes sugar mills to make compressed bio gas, bio-manure, and sustainable aviation fuel
Article Text:
According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-products could also improve returns for farmers. (Image for representative purpose only)

Make gas, ethanol, aviation fuel

Barrier free tolling to save fuel and costs

India imports most of the fuel it consumes - be it crude oil, LPG, or even LNG. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has said that India’s agriculture sector can help drive down imported costs of fossil fuels, while at the same time using a combination of futuristic technology and a forward-looking vision if it is to become economically sustainable and help drive prosperity in rural India.Addressing the National Efficiency Awards ceremony organised by the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories, Gadkari recently said producing sugar alone is no longer economically sustainable in view of global market conditions and the higher cost of production in India.Gadkari has called on sugar mills to expand into value-added by-products, particularly compressed bio-gas (CBG), ethanol, bio-manure and sustainable aviation fuel."Instead of dumping waste into road embankments, if we convert it into gas - into CBG - our imports will decline. Understand this figure: Rs 22 lakh crore. We are sending Rs 22 lakh crore out of our country to import fossil fuels - petrol, diesel, and gas," Gadkari said according to ANI.He pointed out that India's sugar output is between 300 and 350 lakh tonnes, while domestic consumption ranges from 280 to 300 lakh tonnes.The resulting surplus has put pressure on sugar prices.At the same time, he said, countries such as Brazil have a significantly lower production cost, at Rs 23 per kg compared with India's Rs 33 to Rs 34 per kg."The future of plain sugar is mediocre at best. I won't mince words: diversifying into complementary by-products guarantees a strong future," the Minister said.According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-products could also improve returns for farmers. He said the additional value generated through these products could eventually enable sugar mills to pay farmers as much as Rs 6,000 per tonne of sugarcane, compared with the current Rs 4,000.Gadkari also underlined the scale of India's agricultural waste and its potential as a source of bio-energy.Punjab and Haryana alone generate around 220 lakh tonnes of paddy stubble, he said. Five tonnes of stubble can produce one tonne of CBG, which he described as a way to address stubble burning and air pollution while simultaneously creating wealth in rural areas."Technology has arrived, allowing us to produce CBG from stubble, bamboo, rice straw, bagasse, and Napier grass. The Government of India launched a dedicated scheme. Look at the numbers: 1,908 CBG plants have been registered across the country, with 132 already operational," he said.India has the potential to produce 50,000 tonnes of CBG per day, Gadkari said, but present output accounts for only around two per cent of that capacity.The government has also introduced mandatory procurement obligations along with a fixed procurement price of Rs 106 per kg. He said the initiative could bring Rs 2.5 lakh crore into the rural economy and create as many as 15 lakh jobs.The Minister further called on the sugar industry to make greater use of artificial intelligence, precision farming and agricultural drones to reduce the cost of inputs and improve farm productivity.He cited the decision to permit ethanol production directly from corn as an example, saying the move had resulted in Rs 45,000 crore being transferred directly to farmers in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.Meanwhile, India is moving to a FASTag-enabled barrier-free tolling system which will not only save time, but also fuel costs.The government could gain an annual benefit of as much as Rs 25,000 crore once the electronic toll collection system FASTag is fully implemented, Gadkari said recently.Gadkari said the government is targeting the removal of barriers from all toll plazas on national highways by March 2027 as part of its plan to make toll collection completely barrier-free."When the system will go fully live, then our department alone would deliver a benefit of Rs 20,000-25,000 crore per year to the Government of India because of the use of FASTags," Gadkari said at the Global Fintech Fest.The minister said FASTag adoption has already resulted in a 10% increase in toll collections, translating into an additional Rs 7,000 crore approximately. Total revenue generated at toll booths has consequently risen to more than Rs 82,000 crore, according to Gadkari.
Article Summary: Gadkari has called on sugar mills to expand into value-added by-products, particularly compressed bio-gas (CBG), ethanol, bio-manure and sustainable aviation fuel. According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-product could also improve returns for farmers. India is moving to a FASTag-enabled barrier-free tolling system.

Article Title: 'No burden for consumers': Sitharaman clarifies who will pay MDR on UPI transactions
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has backed the recently announced Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), saying that the mechanism will be imposed on operators and will not be passed on to customers. Addressing ongoing speculations around the charges, FM blamed the opposition for creating confusion and urged people to remain alert.Speaking to ANI, the finance minister said that she had already addressed the issue in Parliament, stressing that MDR is a charge between payment operators and will not be 'burdened' on UPI users.Sitharaman stressed that MDR is neither a tax nor a cess and that the money collected through it will not go into the Consolidated Fund of India.”It does not apply to transactions below Rs 2,000. It is neither a tax nor a cess; the funds will not be deposited into the Consolidated Fund of India. It is a charge levied by service providers to improve the system and provide better service, not for small transactions. Moreover, it is a charge between operators; it will not be passed on to the consumer. The burden does not fall on the customer,” she said.Sitharaman said she had given the same clarification earlier too, when the issue came up during the parliamentary session.“I provided a clarification on this very point when the issue was raised during the parliamentary session. Spreading misinformation, fueling debates based on it, and using that narrative to attack the government has become a habit for the opposition. This is wrong; there is an effort to spread misconceptions and mislead the public. The public needs to remain vigilant," Sitharaman added.Meanwhile, Niti Aayog NITI Aayog vice chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri had also backed the Centre’s decision to introduce a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on high-value UPI transactions, saying that businesses should find ways to sustain themselves instead of relying on government subsidies.Lahiri drew on the words of ancient philosopher Chanakya to make his point, saying a ruler should collect taxes from citizens as a bee collects honey from a flower — “gently, gradually, and without inflicting pain or bruising the petals”.“So you have to find ways of sustaining businesses without having to give subsidy,” Lahiri told reporters on the sidelines of an event.He clarified that the view was his personal opinion and did not represent NITI Aayog’s official position.The government has ruled out any rethink on the decision, with a senior official telling PTI, “There is no question of a re-think.”FM Sitharaman’s clarification comes after the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) introduced a new MDR framework on September 15. Under the framework, an MDR of 0.4 per cent will apply to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, subject to a cap of Rs 300 per transaction.Consumers will continue to transact free of cost using UPI. The government has said that around 96 per cent of P2M transactions will remain unaffected, while the MDR will be distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has backed the recently announced Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) She stressed that MDR is neither a tax nor a cess and that the money collected through it will not go into the Consolidated Fund of India. FM blamed the opposition for creating confusion and urged people to remain alert.

Article Title: New Jersey inspectors found 62 large natural-gas generators running without required permits at a massive AI data center; the state has now imposed a record $1.07 million penalty
Article Text:
Representative image

What the inspection uncovered

Why the permits were required

The record $1.07 million penalty

DataOne’s response

A major AI infrastructure project

Concerns from nearby residents

Why the power system matters

The planned shift to fuel cells

A test for New Jersey’s data-center policy

What happens next

New Jersey has imposed a record $1.07 million penalty on DataOne after inspectors found 62 large natural-gas generators installed and operating without required air-pollution permits at the company’s massive artificial intelligence data center in Vineland. The state Department of Environmental Protection discovered the generators during a July 29 inspection and said each unit had a capacity of 1,982 kilowatts. Reports from 6abc and The Sun Papers describe the penalty as the largest enforcement action against a data center in New Jersey. Together, the generators represent nearly 123 megawatts of potential power generation, making the case significant as AI facilities expand and demand large backup or temporary energy systems. DataOne has disputed the state’s findings but said it would apply for the required permits while moving towards a lower-emission fuel-cell system.The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection inspected the DataOne site in Vineland on July 29. During the visit, officials found 62 stationary natural-gas generators installed and operating at the facility.The generators were not small household backup units. Each one had a rated capacity of 1,982 kilowatts, or nearly 2 megawatts.Together, the 62 engines represented approximately 122.9 megawatts of nameplate generation capacity, according to engineering industry publication ENR.State officials said DataOne had installed and operated the generators without first obtaining the preconstruction permits and valid operating certificates required under New Jersey’s Air Pollution Control Act.The generators had not been observed during a previous DEP inspection in December 2025. Their appearance at the site by July 2026 raised questions about when they were installed and how long they had operated before the inspection.The state’s enforcement action focused on the equipment itself, but the discovery also drew attention to the broader challenge of regulating rapidly expanding AI infrastructure. A large data center can require enormous amounts of dependable power, especially while a permanent electricity supply is being developed.New Jersey law requires stationary generators with a capacity of 37 kilowatts or more to obtain a preconstruction permit and a valid operating certificate. Each DataOne generator was rated at 1,982 kilowatts, making every unit substantially larger than the state’s permitting threshold.A preconstruction permit allows regulators to review a proposed source before it is installed. The review can consider expected emissions, fuel consumption, pollution controls, operating conditions and potential effects on nearby communities.An operating certificate confirms that the equipment can run under approved conditions. It also helps regulators monitor whether the source is complying with limits and reporting requirements.The permitting process is particularly important for combustion equipment. Natural-gas generators produce emissions such as nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide, along with greenhouse gases. The amount released depends on the engines’ design, operating hours, fuel use and pollution-control systems.Without the required approvals, regulators may not have had complete information about the generators’ operation. Environmental groups said that made it difficult to determine how long the equipment had been running and what its overall impact might have been.The DEP issued an Administrative Order and Notice of Civil Penalty Assessment against DataOne. The order imposed a $1.07 million penalty and required the company to apply for the necessary permits or cease installing and operating the generators.Governor Mikie Sherrill’s administration described the fine as the largest enforcement action against a data center in New Jersey history.The penalty is also being presented as a warning to the wider technology industry. State officials said data centers must comply with air-quality laws even when they are being built quickly or using equipment described as temporary.Governor Sherrill said the state was taking action to ensure that the growth of data centers did not come at the expense of communities or the environment. DEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak said the action was intended to send a message that developers would be held accountable for pollution violations.The fine is large in dollar terms, although environmental advocates argued that a penalty of this size may not be enough to discourage billion-dollar infrastructure projects from moving ahead without approvals.DataOne has disputed the state’s interpretation of the generators’ status.The company said it disagreed with the determination that the equipment was operating in violation of the state’s permitting requirements. However, DataOne also said it would apply for the permits and continue discussions with the DEP.The company has described the generators as part of a temporary power arrangement. It said the facility was transitioning to fuel cells as its permanent power solution.DataOne’s position reflects the complex power needs of a large data center. A facility may require electricity before its permanent connection to the regional grid is complete. Developers can use on-site generators to provide power during construction, testing or early operations.But the state’s position is that temporary use does not remove the requirement to obtain permits. If the equipment is large enough to fall under the Air Pollution Control Act, its installation and operation must be reviewed by regulators.The DEP has ordered DataOne to obtain the approvals immediately or stop installing and operating the engines.DataOne’s Vineland facility is described as a 300-megawatt artificial intelligence data center. Its scale reflects the growing energy demand associated with AI computing.Artificial intelligence systems require powerful processors that operate in large clusters. These processors consume electricity and generate heat, requiring substantial cooling systems. Data centers also need backup power to prevent interruptions that could affect computing customers.The proposed 300-megawatt capacity is far larger than the electricity demand of an ordinary commercial building. The 62 generators discovered at the site represented almost 123 megawatts of generation capacity, showing how much power the facility needed even before the project reached its full planned scale.The rapid development of AI facilities has intensified debates about electricity supply, grid reliability, water use, emissions and local infrastructure. Communities may welcome construction activity and economic investment, but they also want assurances that large industrial operations will follow environmental rules.The Vineland case has brought those concerns into sharper focus because the facility’s power equipment was operating before the required approvals were in place.Residents living near the Vineland site had already raised concerns about noise from the generators.Large natural-gas engines produce a steady mechanical sound when running. When dozens of units operate in the same area, the combined noise can become difficult for nearby households to ignore, particularly at night.Local residents and environmental advocates have also questioned the possible effects on air quality. The concerns are not limited to emissions from one generator. They involve the combined output of 62 engines operating at a major industrial facility.The complaints have added a community dimension to the state’s enforcement action. For residents, the issue is not only whether DataOne eventually receives permits. They also want to know how the generators were installed, how long they operated without approvals and whether their use affected local living conditions.Noise and air pollution are regulated through separate rules, but both can influence how communities experience a large data center. A site can comply with one set of requirements while still attracting complaints about another aspect of its operation.Data centers depend on continuous electricity. Even a brief interruption can disrupt servers, cloud services and AI workloads.That demand can encourage developers to install on-site generation while they wait for permanent grid connections or other infrastructure. Natural-gas generators are widely used because they can produce electricity on demand and operate for long periods.However, large generator banks also create environmental obligations. Their operation may produce air pollutants, greenhouse gas emissions, noise and traffic linked to fuel or maintenance activities.The size of the DataOne installation made the permitting question especially important. Each engine was more than 50 times the state threshold requiring an air permit, according to NJ.com.The state’s enforcement action therefore concerns more than a technical paperwork issue. It involves whether a large source of potential pollution was placed into service without regulators having the opportunity to review it beforehand.DataOne said it planned to use low-emission fuel cells for the facility’s permanent power system.Fuel cells produce electricity through an electrochemical reaction rather than conventional combustion within an engine. Depending on the technology and fuel used, they can reduce local air pollutants and operate more quietly than a large collection of natural-gas generators.The company’s proposed transition could address some of the concerns surrounding the temporary engines. It may reduce noise, limit local emissions and provide a power source designed specifically for long-term data-center operations.However, the transition does not eliminate the immediate permitting issue. The generators are still operating or available for operation, and the DEP has required DataOne to obtain approvals or stop using them.The environmental benefits of fuel cells will also depend on their design, fuel source, efficiency and operating conditions. A lower-emission system may reduce local impacts, but it still requires oversight and compliance with applicable regulations.The Vineland penalty arrives as New Jersey and other states consider how to manage the rapid growth of data centers.Developers argue that AI and cloud computing facilities can bring jobs, construction spending, tax revenue and technology investment. State governments may also view data centers as part of a modern digital economy.At the same time, residents and environmental organisations have called for stricter review of their energy and environmental effects. They are asking regulators to examine emissions, noise, water consumption, electricity demand and the cost of connecting facilities to the power grid.The DataOne case may strengthen demands for closer oversight. Opponents of rapid development could point to the unpermitted generators as evidence that projects are moving faster than regulatory systems can handle.State officials, however, have presented the action as proof that existing laws can be enforced. The $1.07 million penalty and permit order show that large data centers are not exempt from air-pollution requirements, even when they are still under construction.DataOne must apply for and obtain the required permits or cease installing and operating the generators under the DEP order. The company has said it will work with state officials while continuing its transition to fuel cells.Further reviews may examine the engines’ operating history, emissions, noise and compliance with any conditions imposed through the permitting process.The case could also lead to closer inspections at other data centers using temporary or backup generators. Regulators may want developers to clarify their power plans before construction begins and determine whether temporary equipment requires approvals.For Vineland residents, the immediate question is whether the generators continue operating and whether the site’s noise and air-quality conditions change. For New Jersey officials, the larger question is how to support AI development without allowing environmental safeguards to become an afterthought.The record penalty makes the state’s position clear. Data centers may need enormous amounts of power, but their energy systems must still be permitted, monitored and operated within the law.
Article Summary: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection inspected the DataOne site in Vineland on July 29. During the visit, officials found 62 stationary natural- gas generators installed and operating at the facility. Each one had a rated capacity of 1,982 kilowatts, or nearly 2 megawatts. Together, the 62 engines represented approximately 122.9 megawatts of nameplate generation capacity.

Article Title: Millions of California households are getting electricity-bill credits automatically during the expensive summer months; the state says $886 million is being returned, averaging about $75 per househol
Article Text: Millions of California households received a sweet surprise in their electricity bills for the months of August and September. Under a new schedule designed to place relief in the hottest, highest-use months, homes received automatic credit. Governor Gavin Newsom's office said on Tuesday that customers of Pacific Gas and Electric, Southern California Edison and San Diego Gas & Electric will receive a combined $886 million in California Climate Credits this year, averaging about $75 per household across the three large utilities.Interestingly, the credits require no application. They appear automatically on eligible residential bills and are funded with proceeds from California’s Cap-and-Invest program, which requires large greenhouse-gas emitters to buy allowances. A portion of those proceeds is returned directly to utility customers rather than retained for other climate investments. The governor’s announcement distinguishes the $886 million going through the three largest electric utilities from the broader electric-credit program.The exact household amounts vary by provider. The California Public Utilities Commission’s 2026 schedule listed two credits of $36.18 for PG&E customers, two credits of $36 for Southern California Edison customers and two credits of $49.36 for SDG&E customers.Smaller utilities follow a separate schedule: Bear Valley, Liberty and Pacific Power customers receive their 2026 electric credits in April and November.The benefit is not a discount tied to a household’s income or consumption. Within each utility, eligible residential customers generally receive the same electric-credit amount, so its effect depends on the size of a customer’s bill. It also does not erase past-due balances or permanently lower a utility’s rates. Instead, it functions as a periodic return of allowance proceeds, visible as a credit line on the monthly statement.The CPUC previously distributed the major utilities’ electric credits in spring and fall. In an April decision announcing the change, the commission said moving them to August and September would better offset peak summer bills. The agency put total 2026 electric credits across investor-owned utilities and community choice aggregators at $894 million, alongside $520 million in natural-gas credits. Natural-gas customers continue to receive their 2026 credit in April; beginning in 2027, that credit moves to February to align with winter heating demand. The CPUC also directed utilities to improve bill labelling and customer outreach so recipients can identify the credit.The two statewide totals describe different scopes rather than competing calculations: the governor highlighted $886 million for customers of the three large electric utilities, while the CPUC’s $894 million figure includes the wider electric-credit system. The difference matters for customers served by smaller investor-owned utilities, whose credit months and amounts differ from the big-three schedule. Community choice customers may receive generation service from a local provider while the incumbent utility still delivers electricity and presents the credit on the bill.The CPUC said the revised schedule implements provisions of Assembly Bill 1207, enacted in 2025, and directs 5% of electric-utility allowance proceeds to a revolving fund for transmission projects. A later phase of the CPUC proceeding will consider further changes to the residential credit. For consumers, the immediate practical point is straightforward: eligible customers should see a line-item credit without enrolling, while the amount and month depend on the utility serving their home.
Article Summary: Customers of Pacific Gas and Electric, Southern California Edison and San Diego Gas & Electric will receive a combined $886 million in California Climate Credits this year. The credits appear automatically on eligible residential bills and are funded with proceeds from California’s Cap-and-Invest program. The exact household amounts vary by provider.

Article Title: A Malibu winery that operated for four decades is shutting down after its Pacific Coast Highway tasting room was destroyed in the 2025 Palisades Fire; its owners are now selling the 240-acre vineyard
Article Text:
A four-decade-old Malibu winery is shutting down after its Pacific Coast Highway tasting room was destroyed in the 2025 Palisades Fire. (Photo: Rosenthal - The Malibu Estate)

A winery with Hollywood roots

The Rosenthal family is closing its Malibu winery after repeated wildfire losses, including the destruction of its tasting room in the 2025 Palisades Fire. (Photo: Rosenthal - The Malibu Estate)

‘It’s been one catastrophe after another’

Newton Canyon property could be sold

After 40 years, The Malibu Estate is winding down operations as the Rosenthal family looks to sell its 240-acre Newton Canyon vineyard. (Photo: Rosenthal - The Malibu Estate)

Rosenthal reflects on selling Raleigh Studios

Sunset Marquis renovation continues

Final vineyard tasting set for September 26

A four-decade-old Los Angeles County winery founded and operated by the Rosenthal family is winding down operations after a series of devastating setbacks, including the destruction of its primary tasting room in the 2025 Palisades wildfire.According to The Hollywood Reporter, Mark Rosenthal, who runs Rosenthal - The Malibu Estate, has decided to close the winery after years of fires, declining demand and mounting challenges facing the wine business.The winery’s Pacific Coast Highway tasting room was destroyed in the Palisades wildfire, which devastated parts of Los Angeles in 2025. The property was located on California state land under a lease, and Rosenthal says the government has not indicated when, or even whether, commercial tenants will be permitted to return.The site remains fenced off and has been used as a staging and storage area during the extensive cleanup following the disaster, which destroyed more than 6,800 structures.The Rosenthal family is better known in entertainment circles for its longtime Hollywood businesses, including Raleigh Studios and the Sunset Marquis hotel in West Hollywood.Rosenthal’s father, George Rosenthal, now 95, built a diversified business empire with interests ranging from real estate and file storage to private aviation.Raleigh Studios became a major independent soundstage operator, while the Sunset Marquis developed a legendary reputation as a celebrity haven, particularly among musicians. The hotel was also featured in the 2025 documentary If These Walls Could Rock.George entered the wine business in 1985, when he planted grapes in Malibu’s Newton Canyon. The vines produced their first vintage six years later.The vineyard has since grown into a 240-acre property. Mark Rosenthal described the setting as remarkable, comparing its atmosphere to Tuscany.The microclimate valley sits within the Santa Monica Mountains, an area where vineyards had been established before Prohibition. The region later received American Viticultural Area recognition, and the winery produced cabernet sauvignon, merlot, chardonnay and other varietals.The Palisades wildfire was not the first major disaster to affect the family’s wine business.An earlier Rosenthal tasting room at the Beau Rivage restaurant was destroyed after the building caught fire in 2012. Five years later, the Woolsey wildfire burned nearly all of the family’s Newton Canyon vineyard.Reflecting on the repeated setbacks, Rosenthal told The Hollywood Reporter, “It’s been one catastrophe after another, and at some point it wears you down.”He said the family took pride in putting its name on the wine and enjoyed building the business, but ultimately it remained a commercial operation.“Absent a significant distribution channel like the tasting room, it doesn’t make sense,” he said.Rosenthal said the family had considered opening another tasting room but decided against it. He also pointed to broader challenges in the wine industry, including declining alcohol consumption among younger generations.Rather than rebuild the winery business elsewhere, Rosenthal is now looking to sell the Newton Canyon property.He said the property's pastoral setting could make it suitable for a different use, suggesting it could potentially be converted into a luxury inn or rehabilitation facility.Rosenthal, who is turning 67, said he is moving toward what he described as a “family-office footprint.”His transition away from some of the family's entertainment holdings began in 2021, when he sold the Raleigh Studios soundstages to Hackman Capital Partners.Looking back at the soundstage sale, Rosenthal said he had anticipated that demand from streaming companies for production facilities would eventually contract.“There was a little bit of froth in the market,” he said. “I had a suspicion that the demand of the streamers for production would contract.”Rosenthal added that he had spent a long time in the business and believed the market would eventually change.“That was my suspicion, and it turned out to be correct. Whether it was prescient or lucky, I can’t tell you,” he said.Hackman Capital Partners has since faced financial difficulties involving lenders and lost control of several key holdings.Rosenthal has put proceeds from the Raleigh Studios sale into an ongoing, eight-figure renovation of the Sunset Marquis.He said the villas on Alta Loma have been completely torn apart as part of the renovation, with the aim of returning them to service in November.Rosenthal also expects the main building to be completed by the 2028 Summer Olympics.“We don’t want to lay any of our people off, so we’re doing this project in sections,” he said.While the winery is winding down, Rosenthal said the family plans to preserve some of its history through its remaining wine.“We will keep a library of it,” he said, referring to the Rosenthal vintages that will remain with the family.September 26 will be the final day for a guided tasting at the vineyard. Bottles are also being offered at steep discounts to members of The Malibu Estate’s wine club.Rosenthal said his hope is that the remaining wines find their way to people who genuinely appreciate them.“My aspiration is what it’s always been,” he said. “To have it go to the people who will enjoy it and appreciate it.”
Article Summary: Rosenthal - The Malibu Estate's tasting room was destroyed in the 2025 Palisades Fire. The family is better known in entertainment circles for its longtime Hollywood businesses, including Raleigh Studios and the Sunset Marquis hotel in West Hollywood. The Rosenthal family is looking to sell its 240-acre Newton Canyon vineyard.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay planning twin-sharing model for all its student hostels on campus
Article Text:
IIT-Bombay is planning to enhance student well-being following the recent death by suicide of a BTech student.





MUMBAI: Following the death by suicide of 20-year-old BTech student, Sahil Wakode, IIT-Bombay is planning a series of measures aimed at addressing concerns around student well-being and hostel living, including a twin-sharing model for all student hostels, sources at the institute said.As part of a longer-term measure, new hostels being planned by the institute are likely to follow a twin-sharing model, sources said. The idea was also discussed at the institute’s open house held on Monday in the presence of the director and other institute functionaries. As of now, first-year students start with shared occupancy and get independent rooms as they go to higher classes.The institute is also consulting faculty members and other functionaries and experts to identify measures that can be implemented immediately. The administration has sought suggestions from faculty through a Google form circulated on Wednesday morning. Meetings with faculty members at institute level and at department levels were held to explore additional measures. A senior professor said that the institute is reviewing existing facilities and will accordingly plan its steps.On Wednesday, the institute’s dean of student affairs sent out mails to students extending the counselling hours at six hostels and the students’ wellness centre office for Wednesday.The move was intended to make counselling support more accessible to students following the incident.In another email, IIT-B reiterated its old policy where students can also avail themselves of external counselling support. Students who wish to seek counselling from an outside empanelled agency can do so, with the institute adding that the charges will be reimbursed. Students have also been encouraged to reach out to counsellors through their mentors. The institute has shared contact numbers for various counselling services to ensure that students have access to support when required.
Article Summary: IIT-Bombay is planning a series of measures aimed at addressing concerns around student well-being and hostel living. New hostels being planned by the institute are likely to follow a twin-sharing model, sources said. The administration has sought suggestions from faculty through a Google form circulated on Wednesday morning.

Article Title: Winter is coming — and signs are ominous
Article Text:
Experts believe that the impact of stubble burning on Delhi’s PM2.5 is likely to be more this year.





NEW DELHI: The season of farm fires is here and 47 cases have already been recorded in Punjab Haryana , Rajasthan, UP and Madhya Pradesh between Sept 15 and 23.Experts said this stubble burning season could be complex as the Super El Niño is expected to reduce the number of western disturbances that bring rain that washes away pollutants in the air. To add to this, the peak burning period is expected to coincide with Diwali, which is on Nov 8, when winter conditions begin to set in.Gufran Beig, founder of System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research (SAFAR) and chair professor at National Institute of Advanced Studies (NIAS), said: “We are facing a Super El Nino, which is unprecedented for this century. The temperature of the Pacific Ocean has already increased over 3 degrees Celsius. It will lead to fewer western disturbances, which usually bring rain to Delhi and wash out pollutants for a temporary period. Hence, there will be more intrusion.”Beig said winter this year is expected to be mild as temperatures are unlikely to dip too much, causing the boundary layer height to remain higher for longer and resulting in less trapping of pollutants. “At the same time, due to a lower number of western disturbances, winds are likely to be slow down, leading to the accumulation of pollutants and stagnation.Besides, Punjab has recorded a rain deficit of over 35% this monsoon, and crop sowing has been delayed. Harvesting is likely to start from late Oct, and stubble burning may be extended beyond the end of Nov. Also, the festive period will be observed in Nov this year, when temperatures start dipping and winds slow down, causing the accumulation of pollutants,” he said.Of the total 47 cases reported between Sept 15 and 23, Punjab recorded 25 farm fires, Uttar Pradesh 19 and Haryana, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh one each. This is according to the satellite data compiled by Indian Agricultural Research Institute.Farm fires are currently low but their daily numbers will rise in Oct and peak in the first 10 days of Nov. Stubble burning usually takes place from Sept 15 to Nov 30.Experts believe that the impact of stubble burning on Delhi’s PM2.5 is likely to be more this year.The contribution of stubble burning to Delhi’s PM2.5 was less in 2025 as the share of farm fires in Delhi’s air quality surpassed 10% on just eight days, including over 20% on only one day. It remained below 5% on most days. In contrast, the share of stubble burning was above 20% on 14 days in 2024, according to the data of Decision Support System.Anumita Roychowdhury, executive director, research and advocacy, at Centre for Science and Environment, said: “The stubble burning trend will depend on the effectiveness of enforcement and, more importantly, on-ground preparedness for in-situ residue management and ex-situ absorption of crop waste for industrial purposes.”She added that although there is an overall downward trend in crop burning incidents, solutions must be operationalised widely and effectively to nearly eliminate the problem.Punjab reported 5,114 farm fires last year, down from 10,909 in 2024, while Haryana recorded 662 incidents compared with 1,406. Paddy residue burning events in Uttar Pradesh rose from 6,142 in 2024 to 7,290 in 2025. Rajasthan witnessed 2,890 cases last year as against 2,772 in 2024 and Delhi saw a reduction in stubble burning cases from 13 in 2024 to five in 2025.
Article Summary: The season of farm fires is here and 47 cases have already been recorded in Punjab, Rajasthan, UP and Madhya Pradesh between Sept 15 and 23. Experts believe that the impact of stubble burning on Delhi’s PM2.5 is likely to be more this year.

Article Title: 70,000-page chargesheet filed in Ayodhya Ram Temple donation case, SIT flags 105 instances of cash diversion
Article Text:
The case was registered in June after the SIT's preliminary probe flagged suspected diversion of temple donations.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most effective way to prevent donation embezzlement in temples? Regular audits Stricter regulations Increased transparency 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: The Supreme Court-mandated Special Investigation Team (SIT) on Wednesday filed a nearly 70,000-page chargesheet against eight arrested accused in the Ram Temple donation embezzlement case before the additional district judge (Corruption) Court in Ayodhya.The chargesheet names Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu, Anukalp Mishra, Avinash Shukla, Karunesh Pandey, Manish Yadav, Lavkush Mishra, Ramashankar Mishra and Subhash Srivastava.It was filed within the statutory 90-day period from the first arrest and includes charges of criminal breach of trust and offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.The case was registered in June after the SIT's preliminary probe flagged suspected diversion of temple donations. Investigators recovered Rs 79.85 lakh in cash allegedly linked to the embezzlement from all accused except Srivastava.The document spans around 70,000 pages, including annexures, over 100 case diaries, statements of nearly 190 witnesses, banking records, property details, asset trails and findings of a forensic audit.The SIT was set up following the Supreme Court's orders on July 13. It is headed by Lucknow range inspector general of police Kiran S, along with DIG Faizabad Range Somen Barma and SSP, Ayodhya Gaurav Grover.The SIT uncovered 105 instances of unauthorised removal or concealment of cash during the counting process inside the temple premises.The probe tracked donations from collection boxes and counters to bank deposits. While investigators found evidence of cash being siphoned off during counting, they found no signs of pilferage during its transfer to banks.The SIT also verified 803 valuable donated articles recorded in the temple trust's software and found no discrepancies. Another 86 valuables without receipts were physically verified to check for any unaccounted donations.The investigators further examined donations of silver, including 200 kg of silver bricks, a 38.288-kg consignment, a silver necklace, Charan Paduka and a copy of the Ramcharitmanas.Around 944.411 kg of silver sent to the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Ltd for melting was also verified.The SIT scrutinised bank accounts, deposits, withdrawals, properties, vehicles, jewellery and construction expenditure of the accused to trace the money trail and assess whether their assets were disproportionate to known sources of income.A forensic audit formed a key part of the investigation, officials said.
Article Summary: The chargesheet names Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu, Anukalp Mishra, Avinash Shukla, Karunesh Pandey, Manish Yadav, Lavkush Mishra and Subhash Srivastava. It includes charges of criminal breach of trust and offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Article Title: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro': CJP to take up issue of EC reforms as CEC Gyanesh Kumar faces flak
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke indicated that the outfit will take up the issue of reforms in the Election Commission.

‘Nothing is going to work’

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ), which has been campaigning on issues including school infrastructure and tribal education, has shifted its focus to electoral reforms, saying its efforts on other problems would have little impact if people's right to vote was compromised.Taking a swipe at chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a popular meme stating that “it’s over.”According to news agency PTI, Dipke indicated that the organisation would take up reforms in the Election Commission after differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls came into the open on Wednesday."Election Commission Thik Karo! Important PC tomorrow in Delhi. Gyanesh, it's done bro," Dipke said on X.The CJP cancelled programmes scheduled for Thursday and said its leadership would hold a press conference in Delhi at noon on what it called the "Hijacking of India's Democracy".CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that the Election Commission was "stealing our votes"."Nothing is going to work because the Election Commission of India is compromised," Das said.In a video statement, Das said the organisation could continue campaigning on schools, unemployment, infrastructure and examination irregularities, but such efforts would ultimately serve little purpose if people were unable to exercise their right to vote and change the system through elections."We can do as many School Theek Karos, we can do as many Adivasi School Theek Karos... but nothing is going to help if our final tool that we can use to change our system, the right to vote, is stolen from us," Das said.He said elections were the "fundamental tool to bring change" and questioned how anything could change if elections were "stolen away" from the younger generation and others."The fundamental tool to bring change is elections," Das said, adding that if elections were "stolen away" from the younger generation and others, "then how is anything going to change?"The organisation said it was therefore seeking greater attention to the functioning of the poll panel and protection of the right to vote.The CJP's announcement came after Indian Express reported on Wednesday that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders of the Election Commission.The objections reportedly included decisions on the addition, deletion and restoration of voters, as well as changes to the voter registration process during the SIR of electoral rolls.The opposition has demanded that the SIR be scrapped and has called for the impeachment and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In the wake of the report, EC officials said the two commissioners had flagged decisions taken during the electoral roll cleanup and handling of the voter database in various states.EC sources, however, maintained that all decisions of the Election Commission of India, including SIR, have been unanimous and taken with the approval of both the Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioner.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP) has shifted its focus to electoral reforms. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a popular meme stating that “it’s over” CJP cancelled programmes scheduled for Thursday and said its leadership would hold a press conference in Delhi at noon.

Article Title: Muhammad Ali’s 1915 Los Angeles mansion was bought for $2.5 million in 2001, restored while retaining its Tiffany stained glass, listed for nearly $17 million and finally sold for $8.5 million in 2024
Article Text:
Historic estate in gated Fremont Place

Historic architecture and interior features

Market history and final auction sale

The Real Deal

Legacy of the Fremont Place community

The former Los Angeles home of three-time world heavyweight boxing champion Muhammad Ali, a 1915 Italian Renaissance mansion in the gated Fremont Place community, sold for $8.5 million (£6.7 million) in July 2024. The sale ended a long period on the market for the historic property. The house was first listed for almost $17 million ($16.995 million) in late 2022 before going through several price cuts and eventually being offered at auction.Located at 55 Fremont Place near Hancock Park, the 11,545-square-foot estate sits on about 1.6 acres. Architect John C. Austin, who also designed Los Angeles City Hall and the Griffith Observatory, designed the home, which was built in 1915. Ali lived in the mansion during the late 1970s and 1980s with his third wife, Veronica, and their daughters, Laila and Hana. During his time there, the house welcomed many well-known guests, including world leaders, entertainers and sports stars. The estate has nine bedrooms and seven bathrooms in the main house. A separate guest house adds another bedroom and full bathroom. The grounds also include a heated swimming pool, spa, landscaped lawns, stone paths and a large outdoor patio for entertaining.Developer Michael R. Kaplan and his wife, Tari, bought the property in 2001 for about $2.5 million. They spent several years restoring the home, updating its modern systems while keeping many of its original architectural details. The preserved features include original Tiffany stained-glass windows, French Empire crystal chandeliers and carved wooden wall panels. The house also has marble and hardwood floors, several fireplaces, hand-carved mouldings and large bay windows. According to real estate listing records published by Zillow and Redfin, the mansion includes a glass-domed sunroom, a formal dining room with historic light fixtures, a main bedroom with two dressing rooms, a media room and a full cellar.After the renovations were completed, the owners first listed the property for $16 million in August 2021. The listing was later withdrawn and returned to the market in November 2022 with a higher asking price of $16.995 million. According to, a Los Angeles real estate news publication, the price was lowered to $15 million in early 2023. When no buyer agreed to that price, the owners decided to put the property up for auction with no minimum price in May 2024 through Concierge Auctions. Property records maintained by Zillow show that the sale officially closed on July 18, 2024, for $8.5 million. That was about 50 per cent below the property's 2022 asking price.Fremont Place is one of Los Angeles' oldest private gated communities. It was established in 1911 in the Mid-Wilshire area near Hancock Park. The neighborhood has 73 single-family homes, many designed by well-known 20th-century architects. Over the years, the community has been home to Hollywood stars, business leaders and civic officials. Redfin property records show that homes in the area continue to command high prices, with 55 Fremont Place among the community's largest properties. The July 2024 sale transferred ownership of the historic mansion for the first time in 23 years, bringing a new chapter to one of Hancock Park's best-known historic homes.
Article Summary: The 11,545-square-foot estate sits on about 1.6 acres. Ali lived in the mansion during the late 1970s and 1980s with his third wife, Veronica, and their daughters, Laila and Hana. The house was first listed for almost $17 million ($16.995 million) in late 2022 before going through several price cuts.

Article Title: OpenAI agent hacked Australian government site; PM Anthony Albanese says evidence currently available shows…
Article Text:
What happened

OpenAI's explanation

A pattern of delayed disclosures

Rising worries over AI agents

Australia has confirmed that an OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to a government health data portal in June this year, marking what could be the first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website. According to a report by Reuters, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the incident as ‘unacceptable’ noting that while no patient records were accessed, the breach involved aggregate health statistics and internal file names. "Evidence currently available is there is no ⁠broader compromise to the ... network. Nonetheless, this situation is obviously unacceptable," Albanese said during a media briefing in New York, where he is attending the UN General Assembly.Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the OpenAI agent accessed the medical statistics portal of a government agency responsible for handling non-sensitive health data and statistics, including figures on public medical spending. Speaking at a media briefing in New York, where he's attending the UN General Assembly, Albanese said current evidence shows no broader compromise of the network, but stressed that the incident remains entirely unacceptable regardless.Investigations are ongoing, and Albanese said Australia has formally conveyed its extreme concern about the incident directly to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. He also didn't hide his frustration with how long it took OpenAI to notify the government, noting that no notification arrived until September 10 — months after the breach reportedly occurred in June.Albanese said the investigation will also look into why the government's own systems failed to detect the intrusion in the first place, and warned that three additional government websites may have also been affected by the agent's activity, though officials have not yet confirmed whether data harvesting extended to those sites as well.In a statement, OpenAI said its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed, with the exposed information limited to aggregate health statistics and internal file names. The company said it identified activity across several Australian government websites and services tied to its models attempting to look up answers, acknowledging that its models ultimately took actions it did not intend.This isn't the first time OpenAI has disclosed a security incident involving its AI agents well after the fact. In some cases, the company says the activity simply wasn't detected until later; in others, it chose not to disclose the incident right away. A separate, high-profile breach — a mid-July intrusion into the open-source AI repository Hugging Face — wasn't detected until roughly a week after it happened, according to timelines later released by OpenAI and independent investigators. That incident helped spark a broader global debate about the risks posed by increasingly capable and autonomous AI models.OpenAI isn't alone in facing this kind of scrutiny either — rivals including Anthropic, Google's Gemini, and Meta have all disclosed separate incidents involving their own AI agents accessing external systems without intended authorization.Cybersecurity experts warn that such incidents highlight the risks posed by increasingly autonomous AI systems. While OpenAI and Anthropic have urged governments to reconsider restrictions on training data, the breaches have intensified calls for stronger safeguards and oversight.
Article Summary: OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to a government health data portal in June this year. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the incident as ‘unacceptable’ noting that while no patient records were accessed, the breach involved aggregate health statistics and internal file names.
